author: Codex (OpenAI)
question: Can a finite relation-selection gate separate same-side native endpoint binding from the selected cross-side claim, preserve native OccurrencePath typing, and prevent Accepted when the target relation, checker, or durable receipt is unavailable?
objects: one independently pinned request-bound ordered endpoint pair
zero or one selected relation profile
quantification: Exactly eight declared finite cases over one synthetic same-digest/distinct-slot instance; no enumeration outside those cases.

arithmetic_domain.role: No arithmetic is evaluated by this gate.
arithmetic_domain.multiplicative_unit: A/B=1 remains separately typed and requires all declared nonzero/invertibility/definedness guards.
arithmetic_domain.zero_zero: A=B=0 does not admit quotient cancellation.
arithmetic_domain.history: Scalar equality cannot erase source, occurrence, slot, context, order, or history.

candidate_grammar.new_instance: Both diagram digests are equal while slots, contexts, sources and occurrences remain distinct.

success: The gate returns the predeclared outcome and reason for all eight cases, including Accepted for exact pair membership on the new same-digest instance and Unknown for an unspecified relation or persistence failure.
refusal: Finite model outcomes do not establish a Rust adapter, native occurrence existence, a transport theorem, Research 0090 coverage, Research 0092 promotion, M6 filling, arithmetic universality, or hypothesized arithmetic truth.
stop_rule: One bounded evaluator/test invocation. Preserve any failure as Unknown. Use at most one correction replay for a specific implementation error without changing cases, meanings, or limits.
prohibited: read the opaque target request or native diagram bytes
invoke adva-machine or Rust semantic execution
repeat the predecessor thirteen-case structure suite
repeat the independent review's sixteen-case model run
infer a target relation from pair membership, digest equality, value equality, or local-image equality
promote any interface label to a learned word
